Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Shaver
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 03/03/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 239 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Judiciary could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, local jails, the district attorneys, the Department of Corrections, the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, and community corrections programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Treadaway
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 03/30/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 423 as introduced (1) removes the current exclusion of the use of multiple award contracts for the purchase of push to talk services and (2) removes the current exclusion of wireless communication services, whether voice or data, from exemption from competitive bid requirements. This bill could increase or decrease the obligations of state agencies by an undetermined amount dependent upon the pricing vendors would otherwise have submitted where contracts are purchased through a competitive bid process.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Treadaway
Analyst: Jessic Perez
Date: 03/31/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 423 as amended and reported by the Committee on State Government allows the use of multiple award contracts for the purchase of push to talk services through state competitive bid law. This bill could increase or decrease the obligations of state agencies by an undetermined amount dependent upon the pricing vendors would otherwise have submitted through a separate competitive bid process.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Committee: Insurance
Sponsor: Rich
Analyst: Julie Knight
Date: 02/10/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 31 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Insurance provides further for the regulation of captive insurance companies. The provisions of this bill could increase receipts to the Insurance Department Fund and the State General Fund by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of fees and premium tax collected, respectively, from additional captive insurers licensed in Alabama and additional insurance premiums written by captive insurers in the state.
Further, this bill establishes a provision for captive insurance companies to apply for, and maintain, dormancy status that may be renewed every five years, which could also increase receipts to the Insurance Department Fund by $300 annually for each captive insurance company that renews its dormancy status. This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of the Commissioner of the Department of Insurance to adopt rules concerning dormancy certifications.
Kerry Rich, Chair
Insurance
